newsitem.title: JAPAN: INSTANT VIEW - Japan's August industrial output.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Japan's August industrial output.

text.p: The following is a selection of analysts' reactions to Japan's closely watched industrial production data for August released on Monday, which showed a month-on-month fall of 1.9 percent.
In a Reuters poll, analysts forecast August industrial output would show a month-on-month decline of between 1.4 percent and 2.4 percent.
TOMOKO FUJII, ECONOMIST AT SALOMON BROTHERS, TOKYO:
"The figure was weaker than our expectations. We had anticipated a rebound in September and October. But these are not surprisingly strong numbers."
The ministry forecast that manufacturers' output would show a month-on-month rise of 0.1 percent in September and a 3.2 percent increase in October.

FUJII: "These numbers are still insufficient for the Bank of Japan to decide on a hike in the official discount rate. The Bank will end up leaving the rates unchanged. The basic picture is that the economy will continue to show only a moderate pace of recovery."
YUICHI MATSUSHITA, STRATEGIST AT NIKKO RESEARCH CENTER:
"Upcoming economic indicators will be mixed. So favourable conditions for the bond market will continue."
"The inventory situation has not improved much. So there is going to be a moderate recovery if the economy recovers, or a very slow pace of recovery at least until the end of fiscal 1996."
YOZO NISHIMURA, ECONOMIST AT BANK OF TOKYO-MITSUBISHI:

"Despite the weak output data, I do not see any chance of the economy going into another slump. Capital investment by companies is still modestly strong and this will offset an expected slowdown in public works spending towards the year-end."
